blocks.path: Blood pressure test
s: A blood pressure test is a simple test to check your blood pressure.
High blood pressure can cause serious conditions such as stroke and heart disease.

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > Why a blood pressure test is done
s: A blood pressure test can check if your blood pressure is too high or too low.

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > Why a blood pressure test is done
s: High blood pressure (hypertension) can cause serious problems like strokes or heart disease, but it does not usually have any symptoms.
The only way to find out if you have high blood pressure is to get it checked.

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > Why a blood pressure test is done
s: Low blood pressure (hypotension) can cause symptoms such as dizziness or fainting.

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > Why a blood pressure test is done
s: You may be given a blood pressure test:

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > Why a blood pressure test is done
s: if a doctor thinks you may have high or low blood pressure

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > Why a blood pressure test is done
s: as part of a general health check

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > Why a blood pressure test is done
s: to check if high blood pressure is linked to other conditions you may have

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > Why a blood pressure test is done
s: if you're taking medicine for a long-term condition

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > Why a blood pressure test is done
s: if you're in hospital to check your health

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > Why a blood pressure test is done
s: if you're pregnant as part of your antenatal care

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > Why a blood pressure test is done
s: It's particularly important to get your blood pressure checked if you're at higher risk of high blood pressure, for example if:

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > Why a blood pressure test is done
s: you're aged 40 or over

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > Why a blood pressure test is done
s: you're from a Black or South Asian background

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > Why a blood pressure test is done
s: you have close relatives who have high blood pressure

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > Why a blood pressure test is done
s: you smoke, drink too much alcohol or caffeine, or eat too much salt

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > Why a blood pressure test is done
s: you're living with obesity

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > Where to get a blood pressure test
s: You can have your blood pressure checked at:

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > Where to get a blood pressure test
s: most pharmacies

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > Where to get a blood pressure test
s: your GP surgery

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > Where to get a blood pressure test
s: some workplaces

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > Where to get a blood pressure test
s: Some pharmacies may charge for a blood pressure check.

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > Where to get a blood pressure test > Free pharmacy checks for over 40s
s: Many pharmacies offer free blood pressure checks for people aged 40 or over.

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > Where to get a blood pressure test > Free pharmacy checks for over 40s
s: Find a pharmacy that offers free blood pressure checks

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > What happens when you have a blood pressure test
s: A blood pressure test usually takes a couple of minutes.
You'll be asked to:

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > What happens when you have a blood pressure test
s: Sit down and roll up your sleeve, or remove any long-sleeved clothing.

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > What happens when you have a blood pressure test
s: Outstretch your arm, rest it on a table and relax.

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > What happens when you have a blood pressure test
s: Have an inflatable armband (cuff) wrapped around your upper arm.

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > What happens when you have a blood pressure test
s: Stay in that position while the armband fills with air – this may feel uncomfortable for a few seconds until the air releases.

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > What happens when you have a blood pressure test
s: Devices can be different but the armband is usually connected to a small machine that shows your blood pressure measurements.

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > What happens when you have a blood pressure test
s: The test may be done a couple of times to make sure the measurement is accurate.

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > What happens when you have a blood pressure test > Checking your blood pressure at home
s: If a doctor or nurse needs you to check your blood pressure at home, they may give you a blood pressure machine to use.
They will show you how to use it.

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > What happens when you have a blood pressure test > Checking your blood pressure at home
s: You can also buy your own blood pressure machine to use at home.
Machines may be slightly different, so follow the instructions on how to use it to record your blood pressure.

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > What happens when you have a blood pressure test > Checking your blood pressure at home
s: Take your blood pressure, make a note of the numbers, then wait 1 minute before doing it again.
You usually do this 2 times, once in the morning and once in the evening.
Your doctor or nurse will tell you how many days you need to do this.

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > What happens when you have a blood pressure test > Checking your blood pressure at home
s: If your blood pressure needs to be monitored for 24 hours, you may be given a monitor to wear at home.
You'll need to go to a GP surgery, health centre or hospital to have this put on and to return it the next day.
Wearing it at home will not affect your daily activities.

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > What your blood pressure result means
s: Blood pressure readings are given as 2 numbers, with the 1st number higher than the 2nd (for example,130/80).

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > What your blood pressure result means
s: The first number measures the systolic pressure.
This is the highest level your blood pressure reaches when your heart pumps blood around the body.

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > What your blood pressure result means
s: The second number measures the diastolic pressure.
This is the lowest level your blood pressure reaches when your heart relaxes between each heartbeat.

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > What your blood pressure result means
s: Your blood pressure is usually considered high if it's either:

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > What your blood pressure result means
s: 140/90 or higher when checked by a healthcare professional

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > What your blood pressure result means
s: 135/85 or higher when checked at home

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > What your blood pressure result means
s: You can lower high blood pressure by making healthy lifestyle changes, such as eating healthily, exercising regularly and cutting down on alcohol.

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > What your blood pressure result means
s: Many people also need tablets to control their blood pressure.
A doctor will recommend the most suitable medicine for you if needed.

blocks.path: Blood pressure test > What your blood pressure result means > Blood pressure chart
s: Use our check your blood pressure reading tool to see your reading on a chart and understand what it means.
